strengths: Novel observation that activation outliers in vision encoders emerge in middle layers (unlike LLMs in early layers), with good empirical validation through layerwise sensitivity analysis, foreground/background experiments, and theoretical justification via tokenization differences

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 5 vision encoders, 4 quantization methods, multiple tasks (classification and retrieval), and multiple bitwidths, with consistent improvements especially at 4-6 bit precision

Excellent empirical analysis in Section 3 establishing clear connection between quantization sensitivity and outlier emergence; Table 1 shows high cosine similarity (0.89) of outlier tokens across images supporting universality claim
Practical, training-free plug-and-play algorithm that integrates with existing quantization methods without requiring model retraining
Demonstration of generalization: prefixes learned on ImageNet-1k effectively transfer to other image classification datasets (Table 4)
Thorough ablation studies confirming necessity of both prefix caching and token deletion components; minimal computational overhead (~0.2% FLOPs)
Clear presentation with good visualizations and comprehensive appendices covering additional experiments and analysis
weaknesses: 'Training-free' claim is misleading: method requires extensive hyperparameter tuning (number of deletions k̃, prefix copies τ, search scope) and sensitivity analysis with ~1 hour search cost per model on RTX 4090; tuning procedure is heuristic rather than principled
Improvements at standard W8A8 precision are modest (CLIP +1.16% avg, OpenCLIP +1.29% avg, SigLIP +0.34% avg, DINOv2 -0.62% avg), limiting practical impact for the most common quantization target

Model-specific behavior undermines generality: different insertion strategies needed for different models (CLIP/SigLIP from middle to final layer vs. DINOv2 only at one layer); SigLIP2 exhibits unexplained anomalously large outliers (148.20 vs. 35-92 for others)
Negative result for DINOv2 at W8A8 (-0.62% average degradation) raises concerns about universal applicability; paper dismisses as 'negligible' without sufficient justification
Latency overhead of 5-6% for CLIP/OpenCLIP is non-trivial; paper claims this is 'not critical' and fixable with hardware caching without providing evidence
Limited theoretical understanding of why middle-layer prefixing works better than early-layer for vision encoders; foreground/background validation experiment only shown for SigLIP-B/16
Hyperparameter choices (k=100, τ∈{1,...,15}) appear arbitrary; no sensitivity analysis or principled guidelines provided for selection without full validation search

Generalization study limited to image classification datasets; robustness to domain shift and applicability to other vision tasks (detection, segmentation) unexplored; unclear how well method generalizes beyond the search distribution

Incomplete comparison with related work: test-time register approach only compared on 2 models in appendix; no comparison with other token-level or outlier mitigation alternatives beyond three base quantization methods

strengths: Well-motivated analysis with clear distinction between LLM and ViT outlier behavior, supported by elegant experiments (e.g., foreground/background study in Fig. 4)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 5 vision encoders, 5 PTQ baselines, and multiple downstream tasks with consistent improvements especially pronounced at 4-bit quantization
Practical training-free approach with minimal inference overhead (<1.5%) that integrates as a plug-in module on top of existing PTQ methods
Solid empirical evidence for three key findings (Section 3): outliers emerge in middle layers, are image-independent, and exhibit high similarity across samples
Extensive ablations and supplementary experiments (15+ appendices) demonstrating robustness and exploring design alternatives
Theoretical insight (Lemma 1) explaining high cosine similarity of outlier tokens through spiked vector analysis
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: core prefix-based outlier mitigation directly adapted from existing LLM work (PrefixQuant, Son et al.); main contribution is domain-specific observation and application rather than methodological advance

Substantial hyperparameter tuning requirements per model-algorithm pair (k, τ, k̃) with ~1 hour setup cost contradicts 'plug-and-play' framing; DINOv2 requires special treatment, indicating limited generality

Marginal improvements at 8-bit precision (Average ∆ ≤ 0.77% for most models, negative -0.47% for DINOv2) where practitioners primarily operate; value proposition weakest in practical deployment regime

Insufficient mechanism analysis: why caching and deletion work synergistically (Table 8 shows independent harm but joint benefit) lacks explanation; design choices (KV cache vs. alternatives, deletion from single layer) not justified

ImageNet-1k dependency limits generalization: prefix tuning uses only ImageNet-1k training split; Table 5 evaluates only on similar vision classification tasks with no truly out-of-domain evaluation; label-free variant only tested on 2 models
Incomplete failure analysis and guidance: negative improvements on DINOv2 at W8A8, marginal gains on well-quantizing models unexplained; no clear guidance on when to apply RegCache

Critical implementation details and ablations relegated to 15+ supplementary sections; code availability not mentioned; some hyperparameter choices appear arbitrary (k=100, τ∈{1,...,15}, 50K reference images)
